Group speech into speaker turns so you can review who speaks when.

Pyannote supplies the speech segmentation used by the diarization runtime. ERes2Net supplies the speaker embeddings used to group those segments.

## Current availability {#current-availability}

The native runtime inventory contains sherpa-onnx-node 1.13.5 payloads for macOS arm64, Linux arm64, Linux x64, Windows x64. This is package availability, not a claim that a test passed on your machine. No admitted native payload is recorded for macOS x64 even though model weights are listed for those platforms.

## Use this model {#use-this-model}

Open **Analyze → Speech → Identify Speakers** on a platform with the required native runtime. Local assistance runs in the desktop editor.

1. Select the conversation to analyze.
2. Install both Pyannote segmentation and ERes2Net speaker embedding through Manage Models; the operation uses the pair.
3. Run locally, review the proposed speaker turns, and apply the wanted results.

This operation also requires [ERes2Net speaker embedding](/reference/local-models/speech-3d-speaker-eres2net/).

## Download and requirements {#download-and-requirements}

Model identity: `pyannote-segmentation-3.0`, version **3.0.0**.

Approximate download size: **5.72 MiB**. Minimum system memory: **2 GiB**. This catalog requirement refers to total memory, not currently free memory. Inference also needs sufficient free memory, and installation needs working space; memory is not a speed guarantee.

Published platforms: macOS arm64, macOS x64, Linux arm64, Linux x64, Windows x64. A matching packaged runtime is also required.

Tools → Model Manager downloads the published artifacts and verifies their recorded SHA-256 digests. Processing uses the installed files locally. Open Storage and verification in Model Manager to inspect notices, repair an installation, or change the storage location.

## What the packaged test checks {#what-the-packaged-test-checks}

Case: `speaker-diarization`; operation: `speaker-diarization`.

Input: A public-domain excerpt from John F. Kennedy’s inaugural address, with a second of silence added at each end, prepared as mono audio at 16 kHz.

The result must contain speaker turns with valid speaker IDs and timing inside the input audio. The exact number of speakers is not prescribed.

The nightly-with-tests package downloads real model artifacts and requests inference through the packaged runtime. Missing native engines fail the case on catalog-supported platforms. These costly checks run separately from the normal browser suite. A passing run confirms basic model execution and usable output structure; it does not establish perceptual quality or accuracy on your recording.

## Review the result {#review-the-result}

- Speaker IDs are groups inferred from the recording, not verified real-world identities.
- Short utterances, overlapping voices, and similar voices can be grouped incorrectly. The test checks valid nonempty turns, not an exact speaker count.
